msContents.summary: MS. Arm. d. 2. Čašoc‘ (lectionary) of the Jerusalem type, with readings for feasts and commemorations throughout the liturgical year. The main copy is tentatively dated to the thirteenth century and ends with an incomplete copyist’s note on f. 258v. A separate memorial on the same folio records Armenian year 808 (1359 CE); if entered in the year it records, it provides a terminus ante quem for the original copying unit. The opening leaves (ff. 6–27) and the supplement now at the end (ff. 259–291) were supplied in the sixteenth century. Later records include a restoration colophon on f. 291v and Galoust’s binding notice of 1674 on f. 290v.

note.p: Decorated opening of the Nativity and divine manifestation. The Gospel of the shepherds begins beneath the headpiece. Matthew’s birth narrative follows at 7vA.
f. 22vB: Second day of Epiphany, assembly at St Stephen’s martyrium
The rubric directs the assembly to the martyrium.
The rubric explicitly numbers the fourth day and directs assembly in holy Sion.
Assembly on the Mount of Olives, followed by Psalm and response cues.
Assembly at the Lazareum is specified before the Psalm cue and Pauline heading.
The day rubric directs assembly at Golgotha.
Eighth-day occasion and assembly rubric, with Psalm and response cues, precedes the Colossians heading.
f. 35rB: Common canon for the holy martyrs
After the circumcision Gospel, a separate direction states that this canon is used for commemorations of the holy martyrs. The dated Peter and Abisolom rubric follows immediately.
Dated commemoration rubric names both saints
Dated commemoration of Anthony. The rubric directs assembly at the holy Anastasis, the church of the Resurrection. Psalm cue, Hebrews and Matthew follow.
The date and royal commemoration survive, with part of the name erased.
Fortieth day of the Lord’s Nativity. The manuscript gives 14 February and directs assembly at the city’s holy Martyrium.
Occasion rubric names the holy patriarchs before the Ezekiel heading.
Small Sunday occasion rubric at the foot of A precedes the Isaiah heading.
f. 44vA: Instruction of those preparing for baptism
Heading for the teaching of those preparing to receive the seal. The first and second lessons are Isaiah and Ezekiel. Further catechetical lessons are interspersed through the Lenten cycle.
f. 45rB: First week of Lent, Wednesday
Assembly at the tenth hour in holy Sion is prescribed.
f. 48rA: First week of Lent, Friday
Small black rubric explicitly names Theodore.
f. 58rB: Second week of Lent, Monday
Rubric introduces the second week and Monday assembly at the holy Anastasis.
f. 62rA: Second week of Lent, Tuesday
Tenth-hour assembly at the holy Anastasis.
f. 66rA–B: Second week of Lent, Wednesday
The weekday rubric begins at the foot of A and continues at the head of B. Tenth-hour assembly in holy Sion precedes Exodus, Joel and Micah.
f. 68rB: Second week of Lent, Thursday
Tenth-hour assembly at the holy Anastasis. The three lessons are Samuel, Proverbs and Jeremiah. The latter closes before the Friday rubric at 73rA.
f. 73rA: Second week of Lent, Friday
Tenth-hour assembly in holy Sion. Deuteronomy, Job and Isaiah are separately headed. Psalm and response cues intervene before the following Cyril commemoration.
f. 76rB: Second Sabbath, Cyril of Jerusalem
Rubric associates the second Sabbath with Cyril the patriarch of Jerusalem.
The rubric appears to read «Երրորդ կիրակին», “third Sunday”.
f. 83vA–B: Third week of Lent, Wednesday
Week and weekday rubric begins at the foot of A, with the assembly directions continuing into B. Tenth-hour assembly in holy Sion precedes Exodus and Joel.
f. 87rA: Third week of Lent, Friday
Rubric specifies the tenth hour and holy Sion. Deuteronomy, Job and Isaiah follow.
Sunday rubric follows John the patriarch’s commemoration in the same column.
f. 100rA: Fourth week of Lent, Wednesday sequence
f. 102rB: Fourth week of Lent, Friday
Friday rubric at the foot of B introduces the next Deuteronomy lesson.
Dated rubric names the Forty Saints. Psalm and response cues precede Isaiah 43:1–3a. Ephesians and Matthew follow.
Rubric explicitly names the fifth Sunday. Isaiah, Philippians and Luke form the Sunday sequence.
f. 113vB: Fifth week of Lent, Wednesday
Weekday and holy Sion assembly rubric precedes Exodus. Joel follows. Psalm cue and supplementary Isaiah and Corinthians readings continue the sequence.
f. 118rB: Fifth week of Lent, Friday
Tenth-hour assembly in holy Sion is directed before the Deuteronomy heading at the foot of B. Job and Isaiah follow.
Rubric explicitly names Gregory and the sixth Sabbath. Psalm cue precedes Wisdom. Acts and the good-shepherd Gospel follow under separate headings.
The rubric explicitly numbers the sixth Sunday.
f. 131vB: Sixth week of Lent, Wednesday
Weekday rubric prescribes the tenth hour and holy Sion. Exodus is followed by Zechariah. The textual break at 132v–133r interrupts this sequence.
f. 133vA: Sixth week of Lent, Friday
Friday rubric specifies the tenth hour and holy Sion before Deuteronomy. Job and Isaiah follow, ending before the Lazarus Saturday directions.
Rubric directs a tenth-hour assembly at the Lazareum. Psalm cue, 1 Thessalonians and John 11:55–12:11 follow.
Palm-day rubric directs assembly at the holy Martyrium.
Directions after Matthew describe going to the Mount of Olives with palm branches at the tenth hour, continuing until the eleventh, then descending to the holy Anastasis with a Psalm cue.
Rubric names the second day of the Paschal fast and directs a tenth-hour assembly at the city’s holy Martyrium.
Rubric directs assembly on the Mount of Olives at the tenth hour.
Weekday rubric specifies the tenth hour and holy Martyrium.
Rubric prescribes assembly at the holy Martyrium at the sixth hour. Genesis, Isaiah and Acts precede the dismissal directions, Eucharistic Epistle and Gospel.
f. 160rB–160vB: Acts 1:15–26. The directions dismiss the catechumens before a fresh Psalm cue and the Eucharistic Epistle.
f. 162rB: Holy Thursday at holy Sion
After the sacrifice, directions prescribe movement to holy Sion in the same hour and use of the same Apostle/canon.
f. 163rA: Holy Thursday evening, washing of feet
Small rubric introduces the evening rite.
f. 164vB: Directions after the footwashing prayer. Directions for the officiant in smaller script, between the prayer and the decorated homily opening on 165rA.
ff. 165rA–168rA: Homily in the footwashing service (Քարոզ պատուիրանին).
The dawn rubric follows the homily. Prophetic and apostolic readings, kneeling-prayer directions and Passion Gospels follow. See the separate vigil beginning at 267vB in the supplied ending.
Kneeling-prayer and assembly directions precede the longer Jeremiah lesson.
New day and assembly rubric directs the morning observance at the holy Anastasis. Psalm cue precedes Matthew’s account of the sealed and guarded tomb.
f. 184rA–B: Holy Saturday evening, Easter vigil
f. 207rB: Easter night at the Anastasis
After Matthew’s final commission, directions prescribe the sacrifice and entry into the holy Anastasis during the same night.
f. 208vB: Easter Sunday afternoon and evening
Extended rubric directs ascent to the Mount of Olives at the ninth hour, prayer and reading, descent to the holy Anastasis, then evening worship in holy Sion.
Psalm incipits replace the full weekday station rubric. Monday is the comparative calendar assignment.
f. 224rB: New Sunday (first Sunday after Easter)
f. 226vB: New Sunday afternoon and evening
Rubric directs ascent to the Mount of Olives at the tenth hour, descent to the holy Anastasis and movement to holy Sion at evening.
Partway down the column, the heading «Աւետեաց Աստուածածնին» names the Annunciation of the Mother of God. Psalm cues precede Proverbs.
f. 231rA: Apparition of the Holy Cross
ff. 231vA–234vA: Cyril of Jerusalem, Letter on the Cross.
The rubric assigns the commemoration to a Sabbath.
f. 237vB: John the Baptist and Athanogenes
The rubric assigns the commemoration to Sunday.
f. 239rA: Zechariah after the fast of Saint Gregory
The rubric assigns Zechariah the prophet to the Sabbath following the fast of St Gregory. Psalm cue and Zechariah heading follow.
f. 241rA: Ark and Temple lesson sequence
f. 244vA: Monday after the Transfiguration, commemoration of the prophet Isaiah
The small rubric «Երկուշաբթի» introduces the Monday sequence.
f. 245vB foot: Rubric on the interval after Vardavar
The rubric assigns the commemoration to Thursday.
f. 247vB: Shoghakat (foundation of the church of Etchmiadzin)
Vardavar fast and Sabbath wording precede the Shoghakat notice and Psalm directions.
Reading after the lacuna: f. 249rA: Matthew 19:24 (partial)–28.
f. 249rA: Bartholomew and Jude the apostles.
Explicit commemoration of St James, patriarch of Nisibis, before the decorated Proverbs opening.
David and James, with Psalm 132 cue before the decorated Second Kingdoms heading..
f. 257rB: James the Apostle and John the Evangelist
ff. 259r–267vB: Lenten Sunday Morning Gospel Cycle
ff. 260vB–261vA: Luke 4:43–5:11. Grabar numbering, corresponding to Luke 4:42–5:11 in common English numbering.
Ornamented division on 284v separates these readings from the Good Friday vigil.

msItem.title: Original copyist’s colophon (incomplete)
msItem.colophon: Փառք սուրբ երրորդութեանն հաւր եւ որդւոյ եւ հոգւոյն սրբոյ, այժմ եւ միշտ եւ յաւիտեանս յաւիտենից։ Ամէն։ Գրեցաւ կտակս այս հոգեւոր, փառաւոր, դիմաւոր, անձնաւոր, երկնաւոր, լուսաւոր, խնգաւոր եւ խորհրդաւոր, ի կայից կողմանց, ի հարուստ դարաց, ի բարձրագոյն լերանց, ի հեռաւոր ազգաց եւ ազանց, յերփնապայլուն, շքեղափայլ, գունագեղ, բազմերանգ, ծիածան եւ ծիրանագոյն ծաղկանց, յականց պատուականաց եւ ընդ դէմ ոսկեանց: Գեղեցիկ սաթաց, ծովածին մարգարտաց, ժողովեալ, կուտակեալ, բարդեալ, դիզեալ, հաւաքեալ, տստակեալ, ի փունճ մի կապեալ։ Որով բարգաւ…
msItem.note: Column B: The incomplete colophon opens with the Trinitarian doxology «Փառք սուրբ երրորդութեանն …», followed by «Գրեցաւ կտակս այս հոգեւոր …». It breaks off mid-word at «Որով բարգաւ». The surviving text is undated.

msItem.title: Memorial for the priest Margar and his parents
msItem.note: Ի նստել քո յատենի, յիշեայ, Տէր, զՄար[գա]րայ քահ[ան]այ ու զուր ծնաւղսն։ Ամէն։ Ով որ մեզ յիշեայ, նայ Տէրն ամենեցուն զմեզ ու զձեզ յիշեայ յատենին։ Թվ. ՊԸ։

Foot of column A: A separate memorial asks the Lord to remember the priest Margar and his parents. «Ի նստել քո յատենի, յիշեայ, Տէր, զՄար[գա]րայ քահ[ան]այ ու զուր ծնաւղսն։ Ամէն։ Ով որ մեզ յիշեայ, նայ Տէրն ամենեցուն զմեզ ու զձեզ յիշեայ յատենին։ Թվ. ՊԸ։» The date ՊԸ belongs to the memorial. If the note was entered in the year it records, Armenian year 808 (1359 CE), it provides a terminus ante quem for the copying of the original manuscript.
The date recorded in the memorial is Armenian year 808 (ՊԸ), corresponding to 1359 CE; it is not a copying date stated by the original scribe.

msItem.title: Restoration colophon
msItem.colophon: Փառք անպարագիծ էին, այնմ որ ոչ են հետազաւտելի, եւ ոչ զինչէն եւ ոչ զինչ պիտին: Եւ ոչ քանակին, համբարձելոյն յամենայն մտաց սլացման։ Գոհութիւն անզննին գոյին, որ է բան, կնիք եւ սահման։ Նմա փառք յամենայն եղականացս յաւիտեանս։ Ամէն։ Արդ, գրեցաւ քրիստոսահիմն եւ մարգարէաշէն այս տառ ձեռամբ անարժան քահանայի սակաւագիրս եւ կապեցաւ ծախիւք եւ ստացուածովք հալալ արդեանց: Յիշատակ Ամիրբէկի եւ ծնողացն իւրոց Թումաի եւ Խելոքի, եւ կենակցի իւրոյ Արղուն Մելեքի, եւ ծնողաց նորա Շնոհուորի եւ Պարնլուսի, եւ Դիլշատին, ծնողաց իւրոց, որ աւգնական եղէն ի գիրքս։ Գրեցաւ ի վայելումն Յոհաննէսի նորընծ։
msItem.note: f. 291v, main column: Restoration colophon, opening «Փառք անպարագիծ …». It records copying by an unnamed priest and the binding of the volume at the expense of Amir Beg and other contributors. The colophon commemorates Amir Beg, his parents Thomas and Khelok, his wife Arghun Melek, and her parents, whose names appear as Շնոհուորի and Պարնլուսի. The passage naming Dilshat also refers to parents who helped with the book. The book was copied for the use of Iohannes the novice. Baronian and Conybeare assign the restoration hand to the sixteenth century (C, col. 27).

msItem.title: Documentary note concerning a bequest of fields
msItem.note: f. 291v, right column: A documentary note in a later hand. According to Baronian and Conybeare, it records the bequest of fields at Goshters to the church of the Holy Theotokos and St Paul, with contributions from six householders (C, col. 27).

msItem.locus: f. 290v, to the right of the Gospel text
msItem.title: Galoust’s binding notice
msItem.note: Կազմեցաւ թվ ՌՃԻԳ, ձեռամբ անարժան Գալուստի։
f. 290v, to the right of the Gospel text: Binding notice recording that Galoust bound the volume in Armenian year 1123 (ՌՃԻԳ), corresponding to 1674 CE (C, col. 27).
The notice records the binding in Armenian year 1123 (ՌՃԻԳ), corresponding to 1674 CE.

msItem.title: Incomplete inventory of church chattels
msItem.note: f. 5: Incomplete inventory of the chattels of an unspecified church, written in eighteenth-century notrgir (C, col. 27).

supportDesc.extent:
292 folios 9 6.5
Dimensions as supplied by Baronian and Conybeare (1918, col. 26): leaf size 9 × 6.5 inches; written area 7.5 × 4.75 inches.

collation.p: 22 quires, with Armenian quire numerals at the foot of each quire’s opening recto and closing verso. Most of the numerals had already been cropped by the time of original cataloguing. Textual breaks at ff. 99v–100r, 142v–143r, 166v–167r and 248v–249r corroborate four of the losses reported by Conybeare and Baronian. They also report a loss after f. 200. The original colophon breaks off mid-word on f. 258vB. Conybeare and Baronian attribute this to the loss of the following leaf of the original copy (1918, cols. 26–27). The sixteenth-century repairs supplied the opening leaves (ff. 6–27) and the supplement now at the end (ff. 259–291). Conybeare and Baronian report that the supplement was first inserted after f. 169 and had been moved to the end by the time of cataloguing (1918, col. 26). In the present order, Amos 8:9 continues across ff. 169v–170r in the Good Friday office. The two former vellum flyleaves were transferred to MS. Arm. b. 1.
The contents examination also records a textual break at ff. 132v–133r, between incomplete Zechariah 9:9–10a and Ezekiel 37:10b–14. No cause or number of missing leaves is specified.
For the catalogue-reported loss after f. 200, the present contents sequence records Ezekiel 37:1–14 across ff. 200rB–201rA. The catalogue report is not treated as a separately verified loss.
Baronian and Conybeare identify the former vellum flyleaves as ff. 3 and 16 of MS. Arm. b. 1 (no. 45; col. 27).

supportDesc.condition: The folios show wear and discolouration along the edges, with small perforations near the top of the space between the columns. Paper repairs are visible along the inner margin of f. 237r. Some headings have faded, including the red rubric on f. 235r. The main text is generally legible. The original section has textual breaks after ff. 99v, 142v, 166v and 248v. Trimming of the lower margins has removed most of the Armenian quire numerals.

layoutDesc.layout: Two columns of 24 or 25 lines each. 7.5 4.75
The final reading continues from f. 290rB to f. 291r, where the text is in a single column.

handDesc.handNote: The main copy is written in large, elegant bolorgir, tentatively dated to the thirteenth century by Conybeare and Baronian. Words are generally separated. Alongside contractions of sacred words, the catalogue notes contractions of վասն and the ending -թիւն (1918, col. 26).
A smaller hand entered the memorial dated Armenian year 808 (1359 CE) at the foot of f. 258vA.

The supplied leaves (ff. 6–27 and 259–291) belong to the sixteenth-century restoration. On f. 291v the restoration colophon and the subsequent documentary note occupy separate columns and are written in distinct hands.
The notice beside the Gospel text on f. 290v records Galoust’s binding in 1674.
Conybeare and Baronian describe the church inventory on f. 5 as written in eighteenth-century notrgir (1918, cols. 26–27).

decoDesc.decoNote: Initials and first lines of chapters are rubricated. The headpiece on f. 6v was roughly ornamented by the same hand responsible for the marginal arabesques and other ornaments of the later supplied leaves.

bindingDesc.p: Oriental binding with a flap, formerly fastened with three thongs and three studs. The restoration colophon on f. 291v records that the volume was rebound at the expense of Amir Beg and other contributors. A later notice on f. 290v records that Galoust bound the volume in Armenian year 1123 (ՌՃԻԳ, 1674 CE).

history.origin: Main copy tentatively dated to the thirteenth century. Its place of production and scribe are unidentified. The original colophon breaks off on f. 258vB.
history.provenance: A separate memorial for the priest Margar and his parents at the foot of f. 258vA records Armenian year 808 (1359 CE). If the note was entered in the year it records, it provides a terminus ante quem for the copying of the original manuscript.

The sixteenth-century restoration colophon on f. 291v records copying by an unnamed priest and rebinding at the expense of Amir Beg and other contributors. It names Iohannes the novice as the intended user. Baronian and Conybeare assign the restoration hand to the sixteenth century (1918, col. 27).
A separate notice on f. 290v records a later binding by Galoust in Armenian year 1123 (ՌՃԻԳ, 1674 CE).
history.acquisition: The Bodleian purchased the manuscript from Joseph Bayan on 13 November 1882 (Baronian and Conybeare, 1918, col. 27).

recordHist.source: Description revised by Lewis Read. The earlier description is Baronian and Conybeare (1918), Catalogue of the Armenian Manuscripts in the Bodleian Library, no. 26, cols. 26–27.

availability.p: Entry to read in the Library is permitted only on presentation of a valid reader's card (for admissions procedures contact Bodleian Admissions).
